department: College of Science and Technology (Applied Science and Technology Ph.D. Program)

deadline.value: Applied Science & Technology (AST) Ph.D. admits for Fall only with a priority funding deadline of November 1 and a regular application deadline of December 3.
deadline.quote: Special Case - Applied Science and Technology (AST) Ph.D. program: The priority funding application deadline for the AST program is November 1 and the regular application deadline is December 3.

gre_general.value: The 2025-2026 AST Ph.D. Curriculum Guide lists GRE scores as optional (not required); note that older 2025-26 Graduate Catalog text still lists GRE verbal and quantitative scores with no minimum.

gre_subject.value: Neither the AST Ph.D. page, 2025-2026 Curriculum Guide, nor the Graduate Catalog states a GRE Physics Subject Test requirement.

supervisor.value: Neither the AST Ph.D. page nor the 2025-2026 Curriculum Guide states whether contacting or securing a faculty supervisor before applying is required.

funding.value: Applicants who apply by the priority deadline are automatically considered for Graduate College Doctoral GTAs ($20,000 minimum 9-month stipend, full tuition, and student health insurance for 1 year, renewable up to 2 years, followed by faculty grant GRAs), though currently only a portion of qualified students are funded.
funding.quote: Doctoral Graduate Teaching Assistants (GTAs): doctoral student support will be paid by The Graduate College, and include tuition in the amount for a full time student, health insurance, and a nine month stipend at a minimum of $20,000. This package is a one-year commitment that can be renewed for a maximum of two years. | However, currently only a portion of qualified students will be supported as GTAs.

also.quote: Students who apply late have significantly reduced chances of receiving funding as offers are made to eligible students on a first-come, first-serve basis.

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter directly with a STEM B.S. degree (GPA >= 3.25) or with a STEM M.S. degree (GPA >= 3.0).
entry_route.quote: B.S. degree in a science, technology, engineering, math (STEM) or related discipline with a GPA≥3.25/4.0 or a M.S. degree in a science, technology, engineering, math (STEM) or related discipline with a GPA≥3.0/4.0 from a college or university recognized by a regional or general accrediting agency

notes: Interdisciplinary umbrella Ph.D. with 9 concentrations: Applied Physics (including Nuclear Physics & Astronomy), Applied Chemistry, Bioscience, Atmospheric, Environmental and Energy Science, Data Science and Analytics, Geospatial Sciences, Information Technology, STEM Education, and Technology Management. Fall admission only.
